1.note: It is implied that the army of Baasha first captured Ramah. The full meaning of this statement can be made clear. Alternate translation: [captured and fortified Ramah]

1.q: so that he might not allow anyone to
1.note: Alternate translation: [so that no one could]

2.q: Then Asa brought the silver … of the king’s house, and sent it
2.note: Asa would have had his workers gather the gold and silver for him. Alternate translation: [Then Asa told his workers to take the silver … of the king’s house, and to take it]
This is the name of a man.

This means he spoke by means of his servants. Asa told his servants what to say to Ben Hadad and they did. The meaning of this can be made clear. Alternate translation: [Asa told his servants to say to Ben Hadad] or [Through his servants, Asa said to Ben Hadad] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

3.q: Let there be a covenant between me and you … between my father and your father
3.note: A covenant being between two people represents those two people having a covenant with each other. Alternate translation: [Let us have a covenant with each other … with my father and your father] or [Let us make a peace treaty … with my father and your father]
Alternate translation: [As proof that I want a treaty with you, I have sent]

3.q: Break your covenant with Baasha, king of Israel
3.note: Breaking a covenant represents canceling it and not doing what one has promised to do. Alternate translation: [Cancel your covenant with Baasha king of Israel] or [Do not be loyal to Baasha king of Israel as you promised in your covenant with him]

3.q: Break your covenant with Baasha, king of Israel
3.note: Asa wanted Ben Hadad to attack Israel. Ben Hadad could only do that if he broke his covenant with the king of Israel. The meaning of this statement can be made explicit. Alternate translation: [Break your covenant with Baasha, king of Israel, and attack Israel]
This is an idiom. Here Asa speaks of himself to represent himself along with his army. Alternate translation: [not attack me] (See also: [Synecdoche](ta:figs-synecdoche))

4.q: sent the commanders of his armies against the cities
4.note: Here Asa’s armies are represented by their commanders. Alternate translation: [sent his armies to attack the cities]
These are the names of cities in Israel.

5.note: This phrase is used here to mark an important event in the story. If your language has a way for doing this, you could consider using it here.

5.q: he stopped building up Ramah, and let his work cease
5.note: Here Asa represents himself and his army. “his work” refers to other work that his workers were doing in Ramah. Alternate translation: [he commanded his army to stop fortifying Ramah and doing other work there] (See also: [Ellipsis](ta:figs-ellipsis))

6.note: This refers to all the men who live in Judah. Alternate translation: [took all the men of Judah]
Timbers are large pieces of wood used to build houses or walls.
Here “Baasha” refers to his workers. Alternate translation: [Baasha’s workers had been]
Here “King Asa” represents his workers. Alternate translation: [Then King Asa had his workers use]
This is the name of a city.

7.note: This is the name of a man.
Here the king’s “hand” refers to his control. This means that his army was unable to conquer the king of Aram’s army. Alternate translation: [from you] or [from your control]

8.q: Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a huge army, with very many chariots and horsemen?
8.note: Hanani uses this rhetorical question to remind Asa of a previous victory. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [The Cushites and the Libyans were a huge army, with very many chariots and horsemen.]
This means that king Asa’s army was able to defeat the opposing army. Alternate translation: [he gave your army victory]

9.q: the eyes of Yahweh run everywhere throughout the whole earth
9.note: This speaks of Yahweh seeing everything that happens everywhere as if his eyes were a person that ran all over the earth. Alternate translation: [Yahweh sees what is happening all over the earth] (See also: [Personification](ta:figs-personification))

9.q: so that he might show himself strong on behalf of
9.note: This means that Yahweh shows people that he is strong by protecting his people. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh protects with his strength] or [so that he may show his strength by protecting]

9.q: those whose hearts are perfect toward him
9.note: This speaks of a people’s will and desires as their “hearts.” To be “perfect toward” something means to be completely devoted to that person or thing. Alternate translation: [those who are completely committed to following him] or [those who are completely devoted to following him] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

11.note: This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [from the first thing that he did to the last thing that he did] or [everything he did]

11.q: the book of the kings of Judah and Israel
11.note: This is a book that no longer exists.

12.q: Asa was afflicted with a disease in his feet
12.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Asa had a disease in his feet]

13.q: Asa slept with his ancestors, dying in
13.note: The phrase “slept with his ancestors” is a euphemism for dying. Alternate translation: [Asa died during]

13.q: in the forty-first year of his reign
13.note: “in year 41 of his reign” or “when he reigned almost 41 years” (See also: [Numbers](ta:translate-numbers))

14.q: which he had dug out for himself
14.note: Asa would have had his workers prepare his tomb for him. Alternate translation: [which his workers had dug out for him]
A bier is a table on which a dead body is placed at a funeral.

14.q: sweet odors and various kinds of spices prepared by skilled perfumers
14.note: Putting plants that smell good with the dead body was one of the burial customs of the people of Israel. Alternate translation: [sweet smelling plants prepared by people skilled in this custom]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that skilled perfumers had prepared]
